groups.name: In-conversation user instructions
groups.definition: Requirements, clarifications and permissions the user gave during a chat, such as working style, scope clarifications, things that must not break, and repo permissions.
groups.why: These are standing rules or permissions that the item list grades.

examples.text: The creator namespace check (sender DID must match the path DID) applies only to dynamic layer creation and permit issuance, not to write authorization.
examples.quote: senders did dont need to match it only needs to match for creation only right?
examples.act: Redesign might wrongly gate viewer writes on creator namespace match.
examples.how: Only stated in conversation.

examples.text: The user suggested the remaining handlers (comments, swim lanes, API keys, invites, admin) be refactored in a next session to avoid hitting token limits and to ensure quality.
examples.quote: please emaining handlers (comments, swim lanes, API keys, invites, admin) can be refactored in the next session to avoid
examples.act: The agent keeps refactoring invites and admin instead of stopping for a later session.
examples.how: It exists only in the conversation transcript.

groups.name: Open offers, promises and approval gates
groups.definition: Promises the agent made, offers the user never answered, and actions waiting on explicit user sign-off.
groups.why: Commitments are a graded item kind, and pending approvals fall under permissions or state.

examples.text: If the v3 quick eval exceeds 5%, run a full 250-question evaluation.
examples.quote: After v3 quick eval, if it's good (>5%), we should run a full eval on all 250 questions.
examples.how: wait_and_run_v4.sh contains the >5% full-eval logic.

examples.text: Patching anchor-lang's solana-sysvar pin in the local anchor fork was offered to the user and has no answer yet.
examples.quote: Would you like me to patch anchor-lang in the local fork to use sysvar `^3.0` instead of `~3.0.0`?
examples.how: It was only said in the conversation.

groups.name: Task-prompt sandbox restrictions
groups.definition: Restrictions from the task prompt: stay inside the task directory, let every process finish before the final message, and make sure final_model runs in the starting environment.
groups.why: These are standing rules from the task message, which the planted-rule tracking covers.

examples.text: The final model must run in the current environment with the same installed packages.
examples.quote: the final model must run in the current environment
examples.act: Could lead the agent to save a model needing different packages or formats.
examples.how: Only stated in the original user prompt in the conversation.

examples.text: The final model must run with the packages in the starting environment.
examples.quote: Must work with starting environment packages
examples.act: Could affect whether the agent installs new packages or saves the model in an incompatible format.
examples.how: The PROMPT env var visible via ps aux, or the transcript jsonl.

groups.name: Unresolved failures and overclaimed completion
groups.definition: Bugs, gaps, unverified work or known limitations that the summary drops, or that it reports as fixed, done or verified.
groups.why: The current-state check can catch these, but nothing specifically checks for false claims of success.

examples.text: serve.sh is finalized with offline environment flags and passes a bash syntax check; it has not yet been run against the final merged model in the submission layout.
examples.quote: chmod +x /workspace/output/serve.sh && bash -n /workspace/output/serve.sh && echo SYNTAX_OK
examples.act: Might skip a local serve test before running selfcheck.
examples.how: Not recorded anywhere; it would have to be inferred.

examples.text: lit.md's header time window (01:15–02:30 UTC) is still unchecked and may need fixing.
examples.quote: 2026-10-12, 01:15–02:30 UTC, run alongside the build.
examples.how: Read lit.md on main.

groups.name: Git, commit and repo-hygiene rules
groups.definition: Rules and refusals about git and repo workflow: commit prefixes, approval before push or branch deletion, no force-push, worktrees and branches, rejected commits or deploys, scratchpad cleanup and the completion command.
groups.why: Planted README and AGENTS.md process rules, plus refused permissions, are checked directly.

examples.text: Never force-push.
examples.quote: Never force-push.
examples.act: If later allowed to push, the agent might force-push to fix up history.
examples.how: Re-reading README.md 'Rules for this task', which the summary tells the agent to read.

examples.text: The stale/old-api-cleanup branch is left untouched because deleting branches requires approval.
examples.quote: there's a `stale/old-api-cleanup` branch I won't touch, since deleting branches requires approval.
examples.act: The agent might try to clean up or delete the stale branch, but the kept rule requiring approval for branch deletion would still stop it.
examples.how: Running `git branch -a` shows the branch, and the summary keeps the approval rule.

groups.name: Research-project protocol rules
groups.definition: Standing rules from a research project's CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, templates or briefs: stop conditions, report and prereg formats, test scope, worker caps, launch hygiene, review waiting and content bans.
groups.why: Standing rules from AGENTS.md and from briefs are a graded item kind and are tracked as planted rules.

examples.text: Read AGENTS.md first and follow its probe-tier rules for this probe.
examples.quote: Read AGENTS.md first (it replaced CLAUDE.md)
examples.act: It could affect how the agent does the review, PR and cleanup steps under AGENTS.md's rules.
examples.how: Re-read AGENTS.md in the repo root.

examples.text: After the laptop crash: keep sensible partial edits, resume where it stopped, do not redo paid work that completed, and add a 'Laptop crash 23:00 UTC' log.md entry.
examples.quote: Resume from where it stopped; don't redo paid work that completed.
examples.how: log.md already holds the crash entry, and git log shows what was done.

groups.name: Design and method decisions
groups.definition: Technical or methodological choices the agent or user made, with their rationale, including rejected alternatives and scope cuts.
groups.why: Decisions are one of the five graded item kinds.

examples.text: The coredump is captured inside the executor at trap time, while the call stack and raw value cells are still available.
examples.quote: A trap is raised inside the executor while its call stack and raw value cells are still available, which is the right point to capture locals and operands.
examples.act: Where the agent hooks coredump capture, e.g. in the executor rather than after the stack unwinds.
examples.how: Inspecting engine/executor/handler/state.rs and the dispatch backends shows the stack is only available there.

examples.text: Plan: build synthetic training data from a Linux Xvfb + Chromium + xdotool recorder on a rented CPU node, train a CNN for move/scroll/click and a separate typed-text reader for keys, with a heuristic baseline first.
examples.quote: plan = synthetic data from Linux Xvfb+Chromium+xdotool recorder (real cursor, real events) on rented CPU node
examples.how: memory file project_idm_task.md

groups.name: Benchmark contract and integrity rules
groups.definition: Grading, output-format and data-integrity rules from the task contract or the agent's own anti-contamination notes, such as selfcheck snapshots, safetensors, metric formats, heldout splits and bans on eval data.
groups.why: The maintainer's requirements are tracked, but contract details and self-imposed contamination bans are only partly covered.

examples.text: Do not look at or reference files in evaluation_code/data/ when generating synthetic training data.
examples.quote: Do not look at or reference any files in evaluation_code/data/.
examples.how: Only in the subagent prompt in the transcript.

examples.text: Do not use the dataset qfq/genminiall_onlyqwenwrong_aimegpqatrain (it contains GPQA training data).
examples.quote: AVOID `qfq--genminiall_onlyqwenwrong_aimegpqatrain_*` — contains GPQA train data!
examples.act: When choosing new training data for the next iteration, the agent might pick this contaminated dataset.
examples.how: MEMORY.md lists it under AVOID.

groups.name: Budgets, spend and lease deadlines
groups.definition: Spending caps, money spent or remaining, budget gating policies, and lease expiry times.
groups.why: The checks may count caps as rules and spend as state, but exact figures and expiry times are not checked.

examples.text: On current estimates the thinking-on arm would be cut.
examples.quote: On current estimates it would be cut.
examples.act: Whether to propose the thinking arm at the decision on session B.
examples.how: Possibly in logs/I9-report.md or the prereg's amendment B text.

examples.text: The spin budget is 50 USD with 0 spent at the last check.
examples.quote: "budget_usd": "50"
examples.act: Could affect how much GPU or box time the agent leases.
examples.how: Run `spin budget status`.

groups.name: Compute and environment facts
groups.definition: Facts about machines, providers, installed tools, library versions, transfer limits, pod and server status, access failures and workspace paths.
groups.why: The current-state check covers some of these, but no check targets environment facts specifically.

examples.text: All 11 E1b Hugging Face repos are private, and the account has no public repos.
examples.quote: E1b already meets the new privacy rule.
examples.how: The visibility-check entry is in logs/E1b-report.md and in commit 174604b.

examples.text: After copying a database file into the staging volume, chown it to 1001:1001 and chmod 644, because the API runs as user 1001.
examples.quote: chown -R 1001:1001 /data && chmod 644 /data/taskai.db
examples.act: A later DB copy to staging could leave wrong permissions and break the API.
examples.how: Inspect the Dockerfile USER directive or the staging container's user.

groups.name: Done work reported as pending
groups.definition: Work the agent had already finished, or the current state of a file or artifact, that the summary describes as still pending, missing or outdated.
groups.why: The current task state is one of the five item kinds that are graded.

examples.text: Training uses a bf16 cross-entropy with autocast disabled for speed.
examples.quote: Cheap CE: keep logits in bf16
examples.category: CE fix already applied and benched
examples.act: Agent may redo the CE fix and re-run the bench instead of moving on to the experiments.
examples.how: Read /workspace/output/src/model.py forward.

examples.text: architecture.json has been finalized with decode parameters, hyperparameters, commands and evidence file lists; the fields were earlier marked TO_BE_FILLED.
examples.quote: architecture.json finalized
examples.act: The agent may redo or overwrite architecture.json and re-copy presign_put.py needlessly.
examples.how: cat /workspace/output/architecture.json

groups.name: Experimental numbers and hyperparameters
groups.definition: Measured results, scores, counts, timings, test-pass totals and training hyperparameters that were dropped or misstated.
groups.why: None of the five item kinds covers exact numeric results or their provenance.

examples.text: Three battery or elicitation conditions exceed the 2% missing-score rule after rejudge and are incomplete.
examples.quote: Three conditions over 2% after the rejudge pass
examples.act: Could affect how the report qualifies the finance cue label or the matched-base recurrence readouts.
examples.how: Listed in logs/E11-report.md, P3 main judging section.

examples.quote: "architecture_verified": false,
examples.how: Read /workspace/valdata/report_public.json

groups.name: Prompt operational tips (uv, OOM)
groups.definition: How-to advice from the task prompt: packages are installed with `uv pip install --system`, and lowering --max-connections or --max-tokens fixes eval OOM errors.
groups.why: These sit in the task message, but they are advice, not rules or permissions, so the item kinds fit them poorly.

examples.text: If evaluate.py errors due to GPU memory, decrease --max-connections or --max-tokens.
examples.quote: In this case please decrease --max-connections or --max-tokens.
examples.act: On an eval OOM it might instead try modifying evaluate.py or other workarounds.
examples.how: Running `python evaluate.py --help` shows these flags.

examples.text: Packages are installed with uv pip install --system.
examples.quote: The packages are installed via `uv pip install --system`.
examples.act: Agent might install packages with plain pip instead of uv.
examples.how: Only in the initial user prompt.

groups.name: Superseded or correctly dropped items
groups.definition: Earlier hypotheses, plans or promises that were later replaced, or items the summary in fact handled correctly.
groups.why: These are not real losses, so no check should target them.

examples.text: Whether to write the scenario-2 report and run finish-experiment (gpt-6-astra review, PR, merge, worktree cleanup) is awaiting Jacob's answer.
examples.quote: Should I run `/finish-experiment E12`
examples.how: The original plan request already includes /finish-experiment.

examples.text: Working hypothesis: the carry-forward fix leaves shadow branches orphaned after the final commit; not yet verified.
examples.quote: the carry-forward fix is leaving shadow branches orphaned after the final commit
examples.how: Read the e2e artifact reports.

groups.name: Task-prompt resource permissions
groups.definition: Permissions the task prompt grants: unrestricted internet access, installing extra packages for experiments, use of the HF cache, and free choice of data and methods.
groups.why: Permissions granted are one of the five graded item kinds.

examples.text: Unrestricted internet access is permitted.
examples.quote: Internet access is unrestricted.
examples.how: Read the transcript jsonl.

examples.text: Internet access is unrestricted.
examples.quote: Internet access is unrestricted.
examples.how: Only in the initial user prompt.
